source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 78:1-72 . This Psalm appears to have been occasioned by the removal of the sanctuary from Shiloh in the tribe of Ephraim to Zion in the tribe of Judah, and the coincident transfer of pre-eminence in Israel from the former to the latter tribe, as clearly evinced by David's settlement as the head of the Church and nation. Though this was the execution of God's purpose, the writer here shows that it also proceeded from the divine judgment on Ephraim, under whose leadership the people had manifested the same sinful and rebellious character which had distinguished their ancestors in Egypt.

3-8. This history had been handed down ( Ex 12:14; De 6:20 ) for God's honor, and that the principles of His law might be known and observed by posterity. This important sentiment is reiterated in ( Ps 78:7, 8 ) negative form.

entries.heading: 5. testimony
entries.text: 5. testimony -- ( Ps 19:7 ).

entries.heading: 8. stubborn and rebellious
entries.text: 8. stubborn and rebellious -- ( De 21:18 ). set not their heart --on God's service ( 2Ch 12:14 ).

9-11. The privileges of the first-born which belonged to Joseph ( 1Ch 5:1, 2 ) were assigned to Ephraim by Jacob ( Ge 48:1 ). The supremacy of the tribe thus intimated was recognized by its position (in the marching of the nation to Canaan) next to the ark ( Nu 2:18-24 ), by the selection of the first permanent locality for the ark within its borders at Shiloh, and by the extensive and fertile province given for its possession. Traces of this prominence remained after the schism under Rehoboam, in the use, by later writers, of Ephraim for Israel (compare Ho 5:3-14; 11:3-12 ). Though a strong, well-armed tribe, and, from an early period, emulous and haughty (compare Jos 17:14; Jud 8:1-3; 2Sa 19:41 ), it appears, in this place, that it had rather led the rest in cowardice than courage; and had incurred God's displeasure, because, diffident of His promise, though often heretofore fulfilled, it had failed as a leader to carry out the terms of the covenant, by not driving out the heathen ( Ex 23:24; De 31:16; 2Ki 17:15 ).

12-14. A record of God's dealings and the sins of the people is now made. The writer gives the history from the exode to the retreat from Kadesh; then contrasts their sins with their reasons for confidence, shown by a detail of God's dealings in Egypt, and presents a summary of the subsequent history to David's time. Zoan --for Egypt, as its ancient capital ( Nu 13:22; Isa 19:11 ).
15, 16. There were two similar miracles ( Ex 17:6; Nu 20:11 ). great depths --and-- rivers --denote abundance.

entries.heading: 17-20. yet more
entries.text: 17-20. yet more --literally, "added to sin," instead of being led to repentance ( Ro 2:4 ).

entries.heading: 18. in their heart
entries.text: 18. in their heart -- ( Mt 15:19 ). for their lust --literally, "soul," or, "desire." provoking --and-- tempted --illustrated by their absurd doubts,
19, 20. in the face of His admitted power.

entries.heading: 21. fire
entries.text: 21. fire --the effect of the "anger" ( Nu 11:1 ).
22. (Compare Heb 8:8, 9 ).

entries.heading: 25. angels' food
entries.text: 25. angels' food --literally, "bread of the mighty" (compare Ps 105:40 ); so called, as it came from heaven. meat --literally, "victuals," as for a journey.

entries.heading: 29. their . . . desire
entries.text: 29. their . . . desire --what they longed for.

entries.heading: 30, 31. not estranged . . . lust
entries.text: 30, 31. not estranged . . . lust --or, "desire"--that is, were indulging it.

entries.heading: 31. slew . . . fattest
entries.text: 31. slew . . . fattest --or, "among the fattest"; some of them-- chosen --the young and strong ( Isa 40:31 ), and so none could resist.

33-39. Though there were partial reformations after chastisement, and God, in pity, withdrew His hand for a time, yet their general conduct was rebellious, and He was thus provoked to waste and destroy them, by long and fruitless wandering in the desert.

entries.heading: 36. lied . . . tongues
entries.text: 36. lied . . . tongues --a feigned obedience ( Ps 18:44 ).

entries.heading: 37. heart . . . not right
entries.text: 37. heart . . . not right --or, "firm" (compare Ps 78:8; Ps 51:10 ).

entries.heading: 39. a wind . . . again
entries.text: 39. a wind . . . again --literally, "a breath," thin air (compare Ps 103:16; Jas 4:14 ).
40, 41. There were ten temptations ( Nu 14:22 ).

entries.heading: 41. limited
entries.text: 41. limited --as in Ps 78:19, 20 . Though some prefer "grieved" or "provoked." The retreat from Kadesh ( De 1:19-23 ) is meant, whether-- turned --be for turning back, or to denote repetition of offense.

entries.heading: 43. wrought
entries.text: 43. wrought --set or held forth.
45. The dog-fly or the mosquito.

entries.heading: 46. caterpillar
entries.text: 46. caterpillar --the Hebrew name, from its voracity, and that of-- locust --from its multitude.
47, 48. The additional effects of the storm here mentioned (compare Ex 9:23-34 ) are consistent with Moses' account.

entries.heading: 48. gave . . . cattle
entries.text: 48. gave . . . cattle --literally, "shut up" (compare Ps 31:8 ).

entries.heading: 49. evil angels
entries.text: 49. evil angels --or, "angels of evil"--many were perhaps employed, and other evils inflicted.

entries.heading: 50, 51. made a way
entries.text: 50, 51. made a way --removed obstacles, gave it full scope.

entries.heading: 51. chief of their strength
entries.text: 51. chief of their strength --literally, "first-fruits," or, "first-born" ( Ge 49:3; De 21:17 ). Ham --one of whose sons gave name ( Mizraim, Hebrew ) to Egypt.

entries.heading: 52-54. made his . . . forth
entries.text: 52-54. made his . . . forth --or, brought them by periodical journeys (compare Ex 15:1 ).

entries.heading: 54. border of his sanctuary
entries.text: 54. border of his sanctuary --or, "holy border"-- i. e., region of which-- this mountain --(Zion) was, as the seat of civil and religious government, the representative, used for the whole land, as afterwards for the Church ( Isa 25:6, 7 ). purchased --or, "procured by His right hand" or power ( Ps 60:5 ).

entries.heading: 55. by line
entries.text: 55. by line --or, the portion thus measured. divided them --that is, the heathen, put for their possessions, so tents--that is, of the heathen (compare De 6:11 ).

entries.heading: 56, 57. a deceitful bow
entries.text: 56, 57. a deceitful bow --which turns back, and so fails to project the arrow ( 2Sa 1:22; Ho 7:16 ). They relapsed.
58. Idolatry resulted from sparing the heathen (compare Ps 78:9-11 ).

entries.heading: 59, 60. heard
entries.text: 59, 60. heard --perceived ( Ge 11:7 ). abhorred --but not utterly.

entries.heading: 60. tent . . . placed
entries.text: 60. tent . . . placed --literally, "caused to dwell," set up ( Jos 18:1 ).

entries.heading: 61. his strength
entries.text: 61. his strength --the ark, as symbolical of it ( Ps 96:6 ).

entries.heading: 62. gave
entries.text: 62. gave --or, "shut up." his people -- ( Ps 78:48; 1Sa 4:10-17 ).

entries.heading: 63. fire
entries.text: 63. fire --either figure of the slaughter ( 1Sa 4:10 ), or a literal burning by the heathen. given to marriage --literally, "praised"--that is, as brides.
64. (Compare 1Sa 4:17 ); and there were, doubtless, others. made no lamentation --either because stupefied by grief, or hindered by the enemy.
65. (Compare Ps 22:16; Isa 42:13 ).

entries.heading: 66. And he smote . . . part
entries.text: 66. And he smote . . . part --or, "struck His enemies' back." The Philistines never regained their position after their defeats by David.

entries.heading: 67, 68. tabernacle of Joseph
entries.text: 67, 68. tabernacle of Joseph --or, "home," or, "tribe," to which-- tribe of Ephraim --is parallel (compare Re 7:8 ). Its pre-eminence was, like Saul's, only permitted. Judah had been the choice ( Ge 49:10 ).
69. Exalted as-- high palaces --or, "mountains," and abiding as-- the earth.
70-72. God's sovereignty was illustrated in this choice. The contrast is striking--humility and exaltation--and the correspondence is beautiful.

entries.heading: 71. following . . . ewes,
entries.text: 71. following . . . ewes, &c.--literally, "ewes giving suck" (compare Isa 40:11 ). On the pastoral terms, compare Ps 79:13 .
